subject.title: RFC: Standard Hosting Profiles and Ready Check

question: Should OpenClaw core own named hosting profiles and make their predicates authoritative across readiness, status, health, and release conformance?
rationale: Current main does not provide this capability, and accepting it creates durable configuration and upgrade semantics across several established runtime surfaces.

options.title: Accept staged core contract
options.body: Approve the canonical local readiness projection first, then separately approve container, reverse-proxy, node-mode, and release gating with compatibility proof.

options.title: Narrow to readiness schema
options.body: Accept only the canonical condition and aggregation schema while deferring named profile selection and predicates.

options.title: Keep checks downstream
options.body: Reject core-owned profiles and leave topology-specific validation to hosts, Doctor, or deployment tooling.

recommendation.title: Accept staged core contract
recommendation.body: Approve the canonical local readiness projection first, then separately approve container, reverse-proxy, node-mode, and release gating with compatibility proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across the central Gateway readiness and startup behavior that the RFC would extend.
